components.name: Primary button
components.description: Native PrimaryButtonStyle; HTML is a visual specimen using native-point equivalents.
components.css: .ds-primary { font: 600 17pt system-ui; color: #0F0F0F; background: #F2F2F2; border: 0; border-radius: 16pt; padding: 0 20pt; min-height: 52pt; width: 100%; } .ds-primary:active { transform: scale(.98); } .ds-primary:disabled { background: rgb(242 242 242 / .35); } .ds-primary:focus-visible { outline: auto; }

components.name: Secondary button
components.description: Raised neutral alternative; caller determines width.
components.css: .ds-secondary { font: 600 17pt system-ui; color: #F2F2F2; background: #2A2A2A; border: 0; border-radius: 16pt; padding: 0 16pt; min-height: 48pt; } .ds-secondary:active { opacity: .75; } .ds-secondary:focus-visible { outline: auto; }

components.name: Metadata pill
components.css: .ds-pill { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; font: 600 13pt system-ui; color: #F2F2F2; background: rgb(0 0 0 / .45); border-radius: 999pt; padding: 0 10pt; min-height: 26pt; }

components.name: Script panel
components.description: Flat neutral panel containing the current spoken line.
components.html:
Line 1 · Speaker 1

Your voice belongs in the scene.
components.css: .ds-panel { padding: 18pt; border-radius: 18pt; background: #1C1C1C; font-family: system-ui; } .ds-context { color: #9A9A9A; font-size: 14pt; margin: 0 0 12pt; } .ds-line { color: #F2F2F2; font-size: 26pt; font-weight: 700; margin: 4pt 0 0; }

components.name: Recording control
components.description: Red microphone circle and outer ring. SVG is an illustrative microphone; the native app uses the SF Symbol mic.
components.html: <button class="ds-record" aria-label="Record this line"><svg width="30" height="30" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" aria-hidden="true"><rect x="9" y="2" width="6" height="13" rx="3"/><path d="M5 10v2a7 7 0 0 0 14 0v-2M12 19v3M8 22h8"/></svg></button>
components.css: .ds-record { width: 88pt; height: 88pt; padding: 5pt; background: #FF4D3D; background-clip: content-box; color: #F2F2F2; border: 2pt solid rgb(255 77 61 / .4); border-radius: 50%; display: inline-grid; place-items: center; } .ds-record:focus-visible { outline: auto; }

components.name: Native search
components.description: Semantic preview of Discover searchable. Actual field styling, focus, sizing, and keyboard are owned by SwiftUI and iOS; this preview does not define replacement chrome.
components.html: <input class="ds-search" type="search" aria-label="Search your scenes" placeholder="Search your scenes"/>
components.css: .ds-search { color-scheme: dark; font-family: system-ui; } .ds-search:focus-visible { outline: auto; }

components.name: Native sections
components.description: Semantic inventory of the system TabView; iOS supplies the Liquid Glass presentation and responsive placement. Create currently launches a cover, a known native-navigation deviation.
components.css: .ds-nav { color-scheme: dark; font-family: system-ui; } .ds-nav button { font: inherit; color: #9A9A9A; } .ds-nav button[aria-current] { color: #F2F2F2; } .ds-nav button:focus-visible { outline: auto; }

narrative.overview:
Erica's approved reference supplies the identity: charcoal, a soft screen glow, white actions, and condensed titles printed over scene imagery. The interface gives the image room while keeping recording tasks legible and reachable. This is an existing-reference port, with no generated concept seed or catalog-world provenance.

The implemented native system is recorded from `Dubbing/Theme.swift`, `DiscoverView.swift`, `Library/LibrarySceneDetail.swift`, `DubFlow/SectionPickerView.swift`, `DubFlow/ScriptReviewView.swift`, `DubFlow/DubSessionView.swift`, `MyDubsView.swift`, and `ContentView.swift`. Erica's `erica-frontend/docs/style-guide.md` explains the authority; the main app's code determines the values and behavior here. This document records the system, not a finish-review verdict or a claim that every service is complete.
keyCharacteristics: Scene imagery carries color; interface chrome stays neutral.
League Gothic belongs to printed artwork and the wordmark; system type carries tasks.
Native navigation, menus, sheets, and confirmation dialogs frame the workflow.
Real library and saved-dub data determine counts, frames, and availability.

rules.name: The Functional Hue Rule
rules.body: Keep selection white; reserve red for recording affordances and cyan for coaching.

rules.name: The Printed Art Rule
rules.body: Use League Gothic for artwork titles, role-card names, and the Dubby wordmark; use system type for interface headings, dialogue, and controls.

dos: Do reuse `Palette`, `Radius`, `dubFont`, `displayFont`, `.screenBackground()`, and the shared button styles.
Do let real video frames and saved covers carry color and place readable titles on scrims.
Do preserve native navigation, safe-area actions, Dynamic Type reflow, and meaningful accessibility labels.
Do show loading, empty, failed, and unavailable states from actual data.
donts: Don't use League Gothic for interface headings, body text, or buttons.
Don't introduce decorative accent hues into selection or neutral task chrome.
Don't add invented scores, rankings, identities, or service activity to fill the layout.
Don't replace SF Symbols or native controls with emoji, glyph icons, or web-style navigation.
